events.description: Called with the new value each time the user changes it.
events.name: onChange

props.description: The number of text lines the area shows before it scrolls; native shows it on Android only.
props.name: rows

props.description: The look of the field: `primary` on the page, `secondary` on a tinted surface. Defaults to `primary`.
props.name: variant

props.description: True to refuse input and show the disabled style; the field leaves the tab order and is left out of the submit.
props.name: isDisabled

props.description: The visible label; it is the field's accessible name, so a field without one needs the runtime's own name prop.
props.name: label

props.description: The starting value, for an uncontrolled field.
props.name: defaultValue

props.description: Help text under the field, tied to it for assistive technology.
props.name: description

props.description: The current value, for a controlled field; pair it with `onChange`.
props.name: value

props.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form, and the key a form adapter binds.
props.name: name

props.description: Hint text drawn inside the empty input. It never replaces the label: it is gone once the user types.
props.name: placeholder

props.description: True to fill the parent's width, false to size to the content. Defaults to true.
props.name: isFullWidth

props.description: What is wrong, shown under the field while `isInvalid` is true, and read out with the field.
props.name: errorMessage

props.description: True when the form cannot be submitted without a value; the label shows it and assistive technology is told.
props.name: isRequired

props.description: True to show the error state; the field alone never decides, so a form adapter sets it from its validation.
props.name: isInvalid

props.description: True to show the value but refuse changes; unlike disabled, the field keeps focus and is submitted.
props.name: isReadOnly

props.description:
Background layer rendered behind the text input.
- `undefined` (default): renders `Input.Background` when the active
  library theme registers default background content (e.g. `glass`);
  the fallback color follows the variant (primary → field token,
  secondary → default token); otherwise no layer and no wrapper
- custom node: replaces the default layer entirely and wraps the text
  input (wrap content in `Input.Background` to keep absolute-fill and
  clipping)
- `null`: removes the background layer (bare text input root)
props.name: background

props.description: Additional CSS classes for the text input element
props.name: className

props.description:
Additional CSS classes for the outer container that wraps the
background layer and the text input (e.g. `flex-1` in row layouts).
When no background layer is present the text input is the root element,
so these classes are merged onto it instead — root-level layout stays
consistent across themes either way.
props.name: containerClassName

props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.
props.name: id

props.description: Custom className for the placeholder text color
props.name: placeholderColorClassName

props.description:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
props.name: ref

props.description: Custom className for the selection color
props.name: selectionColorClassName

props.description: Styles
props.name: style

props.description: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests
props.name: testID
